newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia to sell 5.4 pct of power giant UES.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia to sell 5.4 pct of power giant UES.

text.p: Russia, seeking to tap new revenue sources, promised on Thursday to issue bonds to foreign investors this autumn that can be converted into over five percent of electricity giant Unified Energy Systems.

The federal government and the company will each put in 2.7 percent of monopoly UES to raise 5.4 trillion roubles ($930 million) destined for the federal treasury, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko told reporters.

"Proceeds from the bonds issued on the state's 2.7 percent stake will be given to the budget as privatisation revenues," he said. "Bonds issued on the 2.7 percent of the company will also go to the budget but as payment of debts owed by the firm."
He said the size of the stake to be put in by UES had not been finalised.
Russia's largest company by market capitalisation and the government owe each other trillions of roubles, part of a national non-payments crisis, but UES apparently will pay its debts first.

For months as cash-flow pressure on the budget has built, UES and government officials have increased their public estimates of the size of a stake to be privatised to 5.4 percent from an originally envisioned 1.5 percent government share.
In January Russia sold 8.49 percent of the company for 512.82 roubles (then $0.0916) per share.

Kiriyenko contradicted earlier statements from UES officials that the company stake for the bond would be covered by as yet unissued but authorised shares. "These are not authorised shares," he said. "There will not be new issues."

UES on Wednesday said shareholders would be called to an extraordinary meeting on August 26 to discuss giving up the right of first refusal to buy newly marketed shares in connection with the bond issue.

Traders said the prospect of new issues to be covered by the bonds could hurt the price of UES shares, which ticked down to $0.4290 at the close of the Russian Trading System from $0.4320 on Wednesday.
UES is the national electricity natural monopoly, with controlling stakes in almost every regional power utility.

It also owns power plants, the national power transmission grid and runs wholesale electricity market, which federal regulators and company officials say will be opened to consumers to increase competition and decrease industrial power rates.

RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) chief executive Boris Brevnov told reporters the company would issue the bonds, not the government, and that a tender for issue managers would be announced next week and held in three weeks.
UES plans to launch an American Depositary Receipt programme to allow foreign trading of domestic shares before the bond issue to improve share price.
The company is in the throws of government-sponsored restructuring aiming to slash national energy prices to industrial consumers and improve cash flows throughout Russia.
Brevnov, an ally of Energy Minister and reform chief Boris Nemtsov, was elected CEO at the end of May. Kiriyenko said the government would keep control of the company.
"We do not intend to let go of RAO UES," he said. President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday signed a decree authorising the bond. ($ = 5,793 roubles)
